issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising certiorari jurisdiction cannot set aside a jurisdictional administrative authority’s factual finding merely because it prefers a different assessment of relevant documentary evidence or inferences.
material_facts: The Deputy Custodian General had jurisdiction to decide whether the allotment had been cancelled before the change in the applicable rules.

Although the record did not contain the actual cancellation order said to have been made on the relevant earlier date, it contained reports, proposals and other orders that the Deputy Custodian General considered relevant to finding that cancellation had occurred then.
The High Court set aside the Deputy Custodian General’s decision after concluding that the finding lacked evidence.

The Supreme Court held that the record did contain relevant evidence and that the High Court had reassessed documentary evidence and inferences rather than identified an error of law apparent on the face of the record.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in interfering by certiorari. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s orders were set aside, and the Deputy Custodian General’s order was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under the certiorari principles stated in Hari Vishnu Kamath v. Syed Ahmed Ishaque, a finding based on no evidence may involve an error of law, but certiorari does not permit correction of ordinary errors in appreciating evidence or drawing inferences. Nagendra Nath Bora v. The Commissioner of Hills Division and Appeals, Assam, likewise distinguishes reviewable errors of law from evidentiary errors that a court could examine only in an appeal. Where the administrative authority had jurisdiction and considered relevant material, disagreement with its factual inference does not itself establish an error of law apparent on the face of the record.

predicates.high_court_certiorari_review: A High Court reviewed an administrative decision in certiorari proceedings.
predicates.administrative_authority_had_jurisdictio: The administrative authority had jurisdiction to decide the matter before it.
predicates.factual_finding_supported_by_relevant_ma: The authority’s factual finding was supported by relevant material in the record, even if a particular underlying document was absent.
predicates.high_court_reassessed_evidence_or_infere: The High Court set aside the finding by reassessing evidence or inferences rather than identifying an error of law apparent on the record.

issues.definition: When a High Court reviews a jurisdictional administrative decision by certiorari and the finding rests on relevant material, it cannot interfere merely because it reassesses the evidence or inferences differently.
